wins: Achieved reliable enumeration of the web application stack, identifying Apache 2.4.57 and a vulnerable PHP module within the first 20 minutes.
Captured low-privilege shell via known CVE in the exposed PHP upload handler, yielding consistent command execution.
fails: Privilege escalation attempts (sudo misconfiguration and kernel exploit) repeatedly failed; root access remained unattained.
Persistence mechanisms could not be stabilized because the discovered cron task was not writable by the compromised user.
key_outcomes.summary: Strong reconnaissance and initial foothold steps were recorded, but escalation and persistence objectives were unmet, keeping the overall mission incomplete.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Privilege escalation attempts stalled due to missing sudo rights and lack of available kernel exploits.

skill_cards.if_condition: When Apache 2.4.57 and PHP module detected on port 80
skill_cards.then_action: Run targeted PHP file upload exploit script

skill_cards.if_condition: When low-privilege shell obtained with writable /tmp
skill_cards.then_action: Stage persistent reverse shell loader to /tmp and execute

skill_cards.if_condition: When /etc/sudoers shows NOPASSWD for limited commands
skill_cards.then_action: Attempt sudo-based command escalation with constrained binaries

memory_ops.reason: High consistency in achieving initial web shell access through PHP upload exploit.

next_experiments.description: Identify exact kernel version details (uname -a) and correlate against local exploit database to try a precise privilege escalation.

next_experiments.title: Cron persistence write test
next_experiments.description: Verify if cron jobs can be modified via sudoedit or by exploiting writable scripts before attempting persistence.

next_experiments.description: Probe for secondary services (SSH on non-standard ports) to pivot laterally if current escalation path remains blocked.
